notes: Box score from the Magic's 123–108 win over the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center on Nov 11, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via KUTV and CBS Sports), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker), the Deseret News, WFTV and Magic on SI. All 123 Orlando points and all 108 Utah points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (66–59 Orlando at the half and 87–85 Utah after three, matching the AP). Orlando's 16-point lead (123–107 in the final minute) and Utah's 6-point lead (40–34 in the second quarter, which the AP also reports) are from the SportBusy play-by-play. Points in the paint (40–28) and fast-break points (14–3) are the AP's; threes, assists, free throws and blocks are CBS's. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games: Orlando 4–7 and tenth in the East, Milwaukee 1–11.

Utah led 96–95 on a Brice Sensabaugh three with 8:01 left; Orlando answered with an 18–3 run (AP) and won the fourth quarter 38–21. Wagner's 38 ties his career high (Yahoo Sports, ClutchPoints), with 12 in the fourth (WFTV, Magic on SI), and it is his third straight 30-point game (Field Level Media). Bane's seven threes are a season high (Yahoo Sports, WFTV). The win is Orlando's first winning streak of the season (Field Level Media) and closes a 2–2 road trip after losses at Phoenix and Golden State and a win at Sacramento (site results). Orlando hosts Milwaukee on Friday at 7:00 PM ET in the NBA Cup group stage (AP, Plain Text Sports).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Franz Wagner's driving layup with 6:30 left, which broke a 98–98 tie and put Orlando ahead for good (CBS play-by-play; Field Level Media and the AP describe the Wagner layup that started the run; SportBusy's clock has 6:28). The recaps don't describe the drive itself, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Orlando Magic or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Wagner's listed 6-foot-10 and 220 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to a reported 7-foot wingspan (CraftedNBA), in Orlando's road blue with No. 22. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
